extracted.intended_audience: aspiring fiction writers (and readers) interested in writing or understanding novellas
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on planning, writing, and polishing a novella (short novel) including target word counts, structural expectations, and practical tips for publication and series use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical length (word count)
rubrics_metrics.description: A novella is a short novel typically ranging from 17,500 to 40,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some authors consider anything under 17,500 words a short story, while others may stretch it to 50,000 words if the story requires it. The key is that a novella should feel complete but not overwhelmingly long.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete story scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A novella should present a complete story: a full character arc, a central conflict, and a satisfying resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novellas offer the depth of a novel in a shorter, more digestible format—ideal for readers who want a complete story without committing to a full-length book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on a single main plotline
rubrics_metrics.description: Stick to one main plotline and avoid unnecessary subplots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of limited length, concentrating on a single engaging arc keeps the novella tight and coherent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character development depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop characters well; character depth is crucial in a novella.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since the story is shorter than a novel, you must achieve meaningful character development without sprawling subplots—well-rounded protagonists and antagonists are important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative structure (beginning, middle, end / three acts)
rubrics_metrics.description: A novella should have a strong plot with a beginning, middle, and end; break the story into three acts: setup, confrontation, and resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a clear premise and outline to ensure each act advances the arc efficiently within the shorter form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the story moves at a steady pace without dragging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pacing must balance depth and momentum so the novella feels neither rushed nor stretched; maintain engagement throughout the limited word count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edit ruthlessly / concise prose
rubrics_metrics.description: A novella should be tight and polished; edit ruthlessly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim unnecessary material and polish language so every scene and sentence earns its place in the shorter form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning: clear premise and outline
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with a clear premise and well-developed outline before writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A solid plan helps manage scope and pacing; choose a compelling premise, pick a genre and theme, and map the three-act arc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate world-building
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide world-building that supports the story without overwhelming the word count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novellas allow for rich world-building (popular in fantasy, romance, mystery) but it should be concise and directly relevant to the central plot and characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format distinctions and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand how novellas differ from short stories and novels by format and features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short story: 1,000–7,500 words (single incident, concise). Novella: 17,500–40,000 words (complete story, deeper characters, structured plot). Novel: 50,000+ words (multiple plotlines, extensive world-building). Use these expectations to choose the right form for your idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standalone vs. series flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether the novella will be a standalone work or part of a series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novellas can be standalone or part of a series, allowing authors to explore a world or characters over multiple stories while keeping each installment concise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketability and publishing advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: Novellas are often easier to market and publish and appeal to readers seeking a complete short-length story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This format is a practical choice for new and experienced writers wanting to practice world-building and character work without the investment of a full novel.
